$comment: The checked-in anon-read surface (#214, epic #203). Every table a replay of
supabase/migrations/ shows to be readable by the `anon` role must appear here with a
scope and a reason, or `pnpm test` fails — see tools/guards/anon-read-surface.test.ts.
The obligation set is DERIVED from the migrations, never declared, so there is no flag
to dodge with: adding `for select to anon using (true)` to a new table fails the build
until that table is listed here. `scope` is derived too — `all-gyms` means the USING
predicate is literally `true`, i.e. ONE anonymous call returns every tenant's rows.
A scoped policy quietly widening back to `using (true)` therefore fails exactly like a
new table would; that widening is the drift that actually happened (the 2026-07-05
health audit certified 'anon reads limited to gym + gym_domain', and 15 more landed
the next day, unnoticed for 27 days).
The publishable key is build-inlined into every browser bundle by design (ADR-0008),
so this file IS the platform's public read surface. Adding a line is a product
`gym_domain` is deliberately ABSENT: #216 took it off this surface entirely. anon now
resolves one known hostname through public.gym_id_por_host (SECURITY DEFINER) and holds
neither policy nor grant on the table, so it cannot enumerate the customer census.

gym.reason: The pre-auth host->brand lookup runs before any session exists (resolveTenant reads id/slug/brand_module_id). Narrowed at the COLUMN grant instead of the policy: anon and, since #213, authenticated both hold only the 9 brand-seam columns — legal_name, owner_user_id and created_at raise 42501.

gym_contact.reason: The public contacto page renders the gym own address/phone/hours. Scoped per gym since #215: the policy is gym_id = (select public.gym_en_peticion()), which reads the x-gym-id request header createAnonClient(gymId) sets. No header (unmapped host) -> zero rows, never an error.
